thread:
emma: FYI running into a weird one in our onboarding sample app. Rerank keeps rejecting vectors even though embeddings endpoint returned what looks like the right length. Happening only in the Go sample.

emma: repro (go):
```go
// using redwood-go sdk v0.7.0
resp, _ := client.Embeddings.Create(ctx, &EmbeddingsRequest{Model: "embed-std", Input: inputs})
// resp.Data[0].Vector reported len 1024 but rerank says 1023
log.Println(len(resp.Data[0].Vector))
```

rafael: which field did the Go SDK expose? we have been renaming `embedding` -> `vector` in some SDKs for parity and that caused a few surprises. Also any chance of an endianness mismatch? Go's binary.Read defaults to native endian.

emma: Go SDK returns `Vector` (slice float32) while JS returns `embedding`. The rerank client expects an array named `embedding`. Our serialization layer for Go marshals as `vector_bytes` (base64 of float32 LE) and the rerank proxy expects little-endian floats.

lin: pinging in: we recently added a fast-path that accepts either `embedding` (array) or `embedding_bytes` (base64) but it's strict about byte-order. If a client sends big-endian floats the last float can appear wrong and the server validation just checks length and fails if it's off by one due to drop on unpack.

emma: i logged raw bytes: len=4096 and len%4==0, but when decoded with big-endian we got wrong values. The Go binary.Read was using binary.BigEndian on our machine because of a mistaken build flag.

rafael: ok that explains the values mismatch, but why did rerank report 1023 not 1024? was the final float NaN or something?

lin: in our python reranker unpack path we do `struct.unpack('%sf' % (len(b)//4), b)` which will raise if len(b) % 4 != 0. If bytes parse but the last float is NaN it might be filtered by normalizer which can drop NaNs leading to shorter arrays. Edge case: big-endian encoding produced a signaling NaN that our normalizer replaced with nothing. Bad.

emma: workaround: i converted vector_bytes to little-endian locally and forced the SDK to emit `embedding` (array) instead of bytes and rerank accepted it. Example quick patch:
```go
// naive decode + fix
b, _ := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(resp.Data[0].VectorBytes)
// force little-endian decode
buf := bytes.NewReader(b)
vec := make([]float32, len(b)/4)
for i := range vec { binary.Read(buf, binary.LittleEndian, &vec[i]) }
// send vec as embedding array to rerank
```

rafael: thanks for the hack. action items from this thread:
- devex: align SDK field names across languages back to `embedding` and `embedding_bytes` for now, avoid `vector` alias until parity plan complete.
- devex: add endianness assertions and tests in the SDKs to ensure little-endian float32 encoding is used for `embedding_bytes`.
- eng-runtime: make rerank validation return a diagnostics object on dim mismatch (expected/got/field/endianness_hint) instead of a single-line error.
- devex-bot: created ticket INF-6012 for SDK parity + endian tests and INF-6013 for rerank diagnostics.

devex-bot: Created INF-6012: "sdk parity: unify embedding field names across languages" assigned to @rafael. Created INF-6013: "rerank: more actionable dim/endianness diagnostics" assigned to @lin.

lin: i'll push a small server-side improvement to include `endianness_hint` and sample bytes (truncated) for debugging. also will make the normalizer stricter about NaNs and return them to caller instead of dropping silently.

emma: validated local change with little-endian decode + explicit embedding array. Rerank now accepts the payload. Thanks. :thumbsup:

rafael: we'll deprecate `vector` in the Go SDK in favor of `embedding` to avoid this class of problems. will post migration note in sampleapp README and the SDK changelog.

emma: leaving this thread as a note for other platforms: if you see strange rerank rejections, check (1) did your SDK change field names? (2) are you sending bytes vs arrays? (3) check endianness of bytes.

emma: closing for now unless someone sees more.
